statement: For every real a>0 and all real polynomials P_1,P_2 with deg(P_1)=1 and deg(P_2)=2, if every zero of L_a(P_1) and L_a(P_2) lies in [-1,0], then every zero of L_a(P_1P_2) lies in [-1,0]. More generally, for every n>=0, a>0, and r in [0,1], the operator T_r f=(x+r)f+x(x+1)f'/a maps every degree-n real polynomial whose zeros all lie in [-1,0] to a degree-(n+1) polynomial whose zeros all lie in [-1,0].
contribution: A complete proof of the frozen claim. The basis product rule gives the exact differential-operator identity L_a((e_1+r)P_2)=T_r(L_a(P_2)); a partial-fraction formula makes T_r f/f strictly increasing between its poles and locates all roots, while a compact coefficient limit handles repeated roots and endpoints. The same proof yields the stated degree-(1,n) strengthening. No novelty or priority claim is made for that strengthening.
